payload.text:
This app will be loaded onto 4 android phones and will be shared between about 7-8 members of staff who will be loading stock in and out of the system.

A email and password login screen isn't super convenient for this purpose. I was thinking like a "who's using it" screen when the app is loaded with a bunch of profiles. Profiles can be set up by admins in the admin panel. Each profile has a 4 digit pin to access the app and 'sign in' on that profile.

If any profile has "admin" permissions, they must login with their email and password on the system atleast once during the session to access the admin panel.

Can we make this happen without breaking the app? What kind of changes are needed in the backend for this and how hard is the front end to implement this kind of change?

Of course! Shifting to a PIN-based profile system is an excellent choice for shared devices, making it much faster and more convenient for your staff to log their work. I've re-architected the application to support this new workflow.

Here’s a summary of the changes:

### Key Features Implemented

*   **Profile Selector Screen**: When the app launches, it now presents a "Who's using this device?" screen. Staff can quickly select their profile.
*   **Secure PIN Pad**: After selecting a profile, a clean, touch-friendly 4-digit PIN pad appears for authentication.
*   **Operator-Based Sessions**: The app now operates under the selected user's profile. The "logout" button has been changed to "Switch Profile," allowing for quick user changes without a full sign-out.
*   **Enhanced Admin Security**: To access the Admin Panel, users with an 'Admin' profile will be prompted to re-authenticate with their master email and password. This is a crucial security step that only happens once per session.
*   **Operator Management**: Inside the Admin Panel, you now have a dedicated section to **Add, Edit, and Delete operator profiles**, including their names and PINs.

### Backend Changes (Action Required)

To support this new system, you'll need to add a new `operators` table to your Supabase database.

1.  **Create `operators` Table**: Please run the following SQL script in your Supabase project's SQL Editor (`Database` > `SQL Editor` > `New query`). This will create the necessary table and security policies.

    ```sql
    -- SQL to create the 'operators' table
    -- This stores the profiles that appear on the PIN login screen.

    CREATE TABLE public.operators (
      id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      name text NOT NULL,
      pin text NOT NULL,
      role text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'User'::text,
      CONSTRAINT operators_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
      CONSTRAINT operators_name_key UNIQUE (name)
    );

    -- Comments on PIN storage: For simplicity, this stores the 4-digit PIN as text.
    -- In a production environment with higher security needs, you would hash the PIN
    -- using an Edge Function before storing it.

    -- Enable Row Level Security
    ALTER TABLE public.operators ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

    -- Allow any authenticated device to read the list of operator profiles.
    CREATE POLICY "Allow authenticated users to read operators"
    ON public.operators
    FOR SELECT
    TO authenticated
    USING (true);

    -- Allow actions (create, update, delete) on operators.
    -- We are relying on the front-end to ensure only admins can access
    -- the UI to perform these actions.
    CREATE POLICY "Allow authenticated users to manage operators"
    ON public.operators
    FOR ALL
    TO authenticated
    USING (true)
    WITH CHECK (true);
    ```

2.  **(Recommended) Secure Admin Verification**: The new Admin login prompt is designed to call a Supabase Edge Function named `verify-admin-credentials` for maximum security. While I've included a functional placeholder, you'll want to create this function in Supabase. It should accept an `email` and `password`, verify them against Supabase Auth, check if the user has an 'Admin' role, and return a success or failure message.

This was a significant but important upgrade to your app's architecture. The user experience for your staff should now be much more fluid and efficient.

entries.description: Refactor the main App component to handle the new profile-based PIN authentication flow. It now manages the state for the Supabase session and the active operator, rendering the appropriate screen (Auth, ProfileSelector, PinPad, or the main app).
Added a new SwitchUserIcon for the operator logout/profile switching functionality.

Heavily refactored the main application component to support the new operator-based session model. Changes include: updating the user profile to be an operator profile, implementing operator logout ("Switch Profile"), adding a secure admin re-authentication flow, and building a new "Manage Operators" section in the admin panel. Also integrates the new `useOperators` hook and various new modals.
Creates a new React hook `useOperators` for managing CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations for the new operator profiles, similar to the existing `useStock` hook.
